name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft tonal patches, long dry cracks and pebbles running across tile borders, mixed with tiles of shallow damp hollows
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-b

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless terrain tile field with a full-width silhouette of 96 px across all 80 rows. It has mottled brown earth, dark crack lines, pebbles and darker damp hollows, and no standing object, front face, edge line, eave shadow or side face. For terrain this flat top-down ground texture is the expected presentation, but by the structural definitions it has no front face, so it reads as a flat top-down surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown packed-earth field with mottled speckle, small pebble clusters and dark hollow marks. It has about 4-5 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no large flat fills. There are no outlines, and the dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so there is no sticker look. The weaknesses: the board shows no clear long dry cracks running across tile borders, only scattered dark pebble blobs. The tonal patches are soft and low-contrast, so the shading reads as one noisy ramp rather than 5-6 deliberate steps. Texture is evenly sprinkled, with little of the per-clump or per-stone shading Beodeul has. Overall the piece is a bit thinner than the paving reference and not clearly richer than the grass reference. It is not clearly Beodeul quality, so with doubt it fails.
